lexical.anchor: mutationOwner stored in records | 0 occurrences — never persisted ... The single most consequential measurement is the last pair: mutation ownership exists only as a computation.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: UNKNOWN-CANDIDATE-GROUP row (S0212) links them via an unrelated third-party analogy (an ECS trusted-snapshot/failure model 'maps extremely well' onto EKS's fold model and grants) rather than a direct claim between fold-mechanism and grant-record. Both are discussed as sibling components of the same EKS architecture (S0203/S0206: persisted arrays transitions[]/grants[], fold-derived state) but no row derives one from the other.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row stating grants[] are themselves derived via the fold mechanism (rather than being a separate persisted, append-only array) would establish a direct relationship.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Event-based approaches are useful when: lineage matters, auditability matters, reconstruction matters ... costs: replay complexity, temporal complexity, reconstruction cost ... Event sourcing is not universally necessary.
rationale_evidence.statement: Event-driven knowledge-system research finds event history valuable for lineage/auditability/reconstruction, but event sourcing carries real costs (replay complexity, temporal complexity, reconstruction cost) and is 'not universally necessary' -- evidence is mixed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: DeepSeek identified: State = fold as one of the strongest common properties. EKS is the clearest: append-only transitions → fold → current state. There is no independently maintained mutable 'current state' that can drift away from the history.
rationale_evidence.statement: State-as-fold is identified as one of the strongest common properties across systems: EKS derives current state purely from an append-only transition log with no independently mutable state that can drift from history; PKS uses append-oriented governed registers; AIP shares the same underlying workflow/state machinery. Classified as kernel candidate C-2, 'State-as-fold / append-only forward-only log' -- said to describe the architecture's state philosophy, not merely its storage format.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Diagnostics are not supposed to become authority ... EKS is extremely clean here: resolver is read-pure; dashboards are derived ... PKS explicitly says projections are regenerable and non-authoritative. ... DeepSeek therefore says: Diagnostics must not mutate authoritative state — ESTABLISHED.
rationale_evidence.statement: Cross-system invariant: authoritative record -> {interpretation -> recommendation; diagnostics -> reports}, with no path back to mutate authority. EKS's resolver is read-pure with derived dashboards/graphs/recommendations; PKS states projections are regenerable and non-authoritative; AIP is weaker but still distinguishes produced records from owned authority. DeepSeek's verdict: 'Diagnostics must not mutate authoritative state — ESTABLISHED.'

rationale_evidence.anchor: What is persisted vs derived ... A clean and unusually disciplined separation. The record holds facts; every interpretation is recomputed on demand. It is the strongest single design property in EKS, and it is what makes the fold trustworthy.
rationale_evidence.statement: Persisted-vs-derived separation: persisted are schema/workItem/workflow/roles[], transitions[] (verbatim, append-only, seq-stamped), grants[] (verbatim, append-only), and every JSONL row; derived-never-stored are sessions{}, each session's state, mutationOwner, workItemState, handoffsTo{}, authorizationLinkage, the authorized boolean, every resolver verdict/reason/authorizationFact, and all lint/check/dashboard output. Framed as 'the strongest single design property in EKS, and it is what makes the fold trustworthy.'

rationale_evidence.anchor: Governance discipline that is genuinely enforced by construction ... refusal, ambiguity, and 'I cannot know' are first-class, tested, non-error outcomes. Very few systems get this right.
rationale_evidence.statement: Eight governance disciplines are made structural, not merely promised: lifecycle ≠ authority (two arrays never merged); absence ≠ permission ('no record = ungoverned = free' is explicitly forbidden reasoning in code); recommendation ≠ decision; observation ≠ verdict (three verdicts are structurally unemittable by machine); discovery ≠ activation (the resolver is write-free by construction, pinned by test T-11); one interpretation authority (the resolver subprocesses fold rather than parsing records itself, T-13); ambiguity is an answer (AMBIGUOUS lists all candidates, chooses none, exits 0); producer ≠ acceptor (the durability ADR binds its own producing process out of approving it). 'Refusal, ambiguity, and "I cannot know" are first-class, tested, non-error outcomes. Very few systems get this right.'

rationale_evidence.anchor: proc_open('php', <script>, 'fold') — the resolver → engine delegation ... the only inter-component protocol in EKS ... No network integration. No API. No serialization contract between components other than the JSON that fold prints on stdout.
rationale_evidence.statement: EKS's only inter-component protocol is a subprocess call (session-resolve.php spawns workflow-state.php fold via proc_open); nine integration mechanisms total are catalogued (filesystem, git CLI, the subprocess delegation, shell_exec/require_once between scripts, Composer autoload, AI-harness hooks, GitHub Actions, the KOS_MECHANISM_PATH env var, and prose cross-references resolved only by humans); there is no network integration, no API, and no serialization contract between components other than the JSON that `fold` prints to stdout.

## Rationale
Event-driven knowledge-system research finds event history valuable for lineage/auditability/reconstruction, but event sourcing carries real costs (replay complexity, temporal complexity, reconstruction cost) and is 'not universally necessary' -- evidence is mixed. [S0202] State-as-fold is identified as one of the strongest common properties across systems: EKS derives current state purely from an append-only transition log with no independently mutable state that can drift from history; PKS uses append-oriented governed registers; AIP shares the same underlying workflow/state machinery. Classified as kernel candidate C-2, 'State-as-fold / append-only forward-only log' -- said to describe the architecture's state philosophy, not merely its storage format. [S0203] Cross-system invariant: authoritative record -> {interpretation -> recommendation; diagnostics -> reports}, with no path back to mutate authority. EKS's resolver is read-pure with derived dashboards/graphs/recommendations; PKS states projections are regenerable and non-authoritative; AIP is weaker but still distinguishes produced records from owned authority. DeepSeek's verdict: 'Diagnostics must not mutate authoritative state — ESTABLISHED.' [S0203] Persisted-vs-derived separation: persisted are schema/workItem/workflow/roles[], transitions[] (verbatim, append-only, seq-stamped), grants[] (verbatim, append-only), and every JSONL row; derived-never-stored are sessions{}, each session's state, mutationOwner, workItemState, handoffsTo{}, authorizationLinkage, the authorized boolean, every resolver verdict/reason/authorizationFact, and all lint/check/dashboard output. Framed as 'the strongest single design property in EKS, and it is what makes the fold trustworthy.' [S0206] Eight governance disciplines are made structural, not merely promised: lifecycle ≠ authority (two arrays never merged); absence ≠ permission ('no record = ungoverned = free' is explicitly forbidden reasoning in code); recommendation ≠ decision; observation ≠ verdict (three verdicts are structurally unemittable by machine); discovery ≠ activation (the resolver is write-free by construction, pinned by test T-11); one interpretation authority (the resolver subprocesses fold rather than parsing records itself, T-13); ambiguity is an answer (AMBIGUOUS lists all candidates, chooses none, exits 0); producer ≠ acceptor (the durability ADR binds its own producing process out of approving it). 'Refusal, ambiguity, and "I cannot know" are first-class, tested, non-error outcomes. Very few systems get this right.' [S0206] EKS's only inter-component protocol is a subprocess call (session-resolve.php spawns workflow-state.php fold via proc_open); nine integration mechanisms total are catalogued (filesystem, git CLI, the subprocess delegation, shell_exec/require_once between scripts, Composer autoload, AI-harness hooks, GitHub Actions, the KOS_MECHANISM_PATH env var, and prose cross-references resolved only by humans); there is no network integration, no API, and no serialization contract between components other than the JSON that `fold` prints to stdout. [S0206]
